statement: With English now so widely used and translation technology improving rapidly, learning a foreign language is becoming a waste of time.
question: To what extent do you agree or disagree?
model:
Instant translation apps and the global dominance of English have led some to conclude that learning another language is now an outdated pursuit. I strongly disagree with this view, because language study offers benefits that no device can replicate.

It is undeniable that technology has removed many practical barriers. A tourist in Tokyo can now read a menu by pointing a phone camera at it, and international business is routinely conducted in English even when neither party is a native speaker. For simple transactions, therefore, the need to master grammar and vocabulary has diminished considerably.

However, communication is far more than the exchange of information. Translation software still struggles with humour, irony and the subtle shifts in tone that build trust between people. A diplomat or engineer who can chat with colleagues in their own language, even imperfectly, signals respect and gains insights that would be lost through a screen. Moreover, a language carries a culture within it: the Portuguese word saudade, for instance, captures a particular blend of longing and nostalgia that reveals something about how Brazilians and Portuguese experience the world, and no dictionary entry fully conveys it.

There are also cognitive and personal rewards. Studies suggest that bilingual people are better at switching between tasks and may even experience a delay in the onset of dementia. Just as importantly, learning a language develops patience and humility, as learners must tolerate making mistakes in public. Finally, relying on English alone leaves native English speakers at a disadvantage, since their competitors abroad typically speak English as well as their mother tongue.

In conclusion, although technology has made basic communication across languages easier than ever, it has not made language learning pointless. On the contrary, in an interconnected world, the ability to understand others on their own terms is arguably more valuable now than at any time in the past.
